The Company remains focused on inventory optimization and working capital efficiency as it prepares to support the expected increased production requirements.

Building on the sequential improvement demonstrated in Q3 2026, the Company expects substantially stronger operating performance in Q4 2026, as stronger bookings are expected to increasingly convert into shipments and ongoing pricing, sourcing and cost-reduction actions support improved profitability.

While customer delivery schedules and sourcing transitions slowed the conversion of higher bookings into shipments, the Company expects this conversion to accelerate in Q4 2026, driving higher shipment volumes, increased revenue, and improved operating efficiencies.
The Company's updated outlook reflects current assumptions regarding tariffs, geopolitical developments and market conditions.

The Company expects bookings in Q4 2026 to exceed Q4 2025 and Q3 2026, supported by improving industry conditions, anticipated market share gains, and broader customer acceptance of its expanded product portfolio.
The Company expects its standard and value offerings in the 1-3.5 ton, 4-9 ton and Big Truck product lines will continue to support volume growth, profitability, and market share gains.
The Company's newly introduced lighter-intensity, lower-priced trucks are expected to broaden its addressable market and support increased manufacturing scale over time.
Overall, the Company expects Lift Truck adjusted operating results to be positive and improve in Q4 2026.
The Company expects demand and production levels to remain healthy in 2027, supported by gradually strengthening market conditions and ongoing growth initiatives.
The Company's previously announced 2024 U.S. manufacturing footprint optimization projects remain on track to deliver increased operational benefits in 2027.

The anticipated savings, which are reflected in the Company's outlook, are expected to substantially offset ongoing cost increases and support underlying product margins rather than translate fully into incremental margin expansion.

statements.t: As of September 30, 2026, substantially all of the Company's backlog is expected to be sold within the next twelve months.

The Company expects future costs and benefits for the projects as shown below:
In Q4 2026, the Company launched a major set of projects expected to strengthen the Company's cost structure, capital efficiency and long-term competitiveness.

The Company's modular, scalable products have created new product opportunities and production efficiencies, which the Company believes provide the foundation for these new projects in addition to previously announced restructuring plans.

These new projects are expected to improve operations and better align the Company with evolving market and regulatory requirements, including significant changes in demand for forklift truck types and volumes.
• reshaping the Company’s product portfolio and route-to-market, including exiting from the hydrogen fuel cell and HydroCharge business and discontinuing plans to manufacture Big Trucks in the U.S.;
The Company is targeting at least $100 million of an annual cost savings expected at maturity in 2029.
The Company continues to pursue the mitigation of these costs and is currently unable to estimate the high-end of the expected implementation costs or segments in which these costs will be recorded.

To preserve cash amid a slower-than-anticipated recovery, the Company expects 2026 capital expenditures of $50 million to $60 million and to limit 2027 capital expenditures to $40 million to $50 million.

Over time, product portfolio simplification, reduced manufacturing complexity and lower capital intensity are also expected to reduce working capital requirements and support the Company's continued target of working capital at approximately 15% of revenue.

The Company expects these projects to strengthen its cost structure while supporting key strategic programs, including modular, scalable forklift truck product solutions for lighter-intensity and standard applications and broader sales coverage across the addressable market.

We have begun to initiate certain projects, while others remain subject to final planning, applicable legal and regulatory requirements, consultation obligations and other customary approval processes.
The Company expects to provide additional information as material plans and actions are finalized.

The Company is focused on executing established strategic initiatives and key projects to transform the Company’s core lift truck business while building new business opportunities in the warehouse lift truck, vehicle automation, energy management and attachment business activities.
These complementary growth and profit improvement projects should help the Company fulfill these two promises while achieving long-term revenue and operating profit growth.
The Company believes key projects will contribute to an increased and sustainable lift truck and attachment competitive advantage over time.
